title: Optimize checkpoint ingestion and tokenizer boundary preservation
creator: Daniel Kim
description: Problem: Our current checkpoint ingestion path has grown organically to support multiple historical weight formats and ad-hoc sharding metadata. This causes repeated runtime conversions, tokenizer/kv-cache mismatches for some legacy models, and a lot of conditional code scattered across the loader. Impact: increased cold-start latency, memory pressure during restore, and difficult-to-reason-about correctness when tokenizer vocab/byte-pair boundary assumptions differ between saved metadata and runtime tokenizers. Goal: Consolidate the ingestion pipeline into a small number of clear stages (manifest normalization, shard assignment, lazy weight materialization, tokenizer boundary reconciliation) with a compatibility shim that converts legacy checkpoints to a normalized manifest on first read. Keep the API surface small and ensure that existing models continue to load without user action. Deliver measurable improvements in cold-start latency and predictable peak memory usage.
acceptance_criteria: New ingestion flow implemented behind a feature flag (ingestion_v2)
Compatibility shim converts legacy manifests to normalized format without data loss (integration tests)
Cold-start wall-clock time for large 30B checkpoint reduced by >=20% on average in our test harness
Peak resident set memory during checkpoint restore reduced by >=15% for sharded checkpoints on GPU hosts
Tokenizer boundary reconciliation prevents at least 2 classes of previously observed tokenization regressions (validated by unit tests + small eval prompts)
All existing model bundles in fixtures load with ingestion_v2 enabled and pass synthetic inference smoke tests
migration_steps: Add ingestion_v2 behind feature-flag and run canary on staging hosts
Run full-suite integration tests with canonical fixtures and legacy bundles
Deploy feature-flag to dedicated infra with telemetry enabled to compare metrics
Gradually enable ingestion_v2 for read-only jobs, then for production read-after-write paths
Remove legacy conversion path after 2 successful weekly runs and deprecate flag
